I remember one specific patient from my clinical days. A 39-year-old manager, at the top of his industry at the time. He was in the hospital, about to lose his leg. And he just kept crying, and lamenting on how a small wound had ultimately resulted in this. Let me tell you how. You see, for the past year, he was managing tiredness all in the name of hustle. According to him, he drank a lot of soda just to hold bodi. And even when he had blurry vision, he always thought it was because of his laptop screen. But the worst part of the scenario was that he was managing a ‘small wound' on his toe that just refused to heal. He didn't know that all those signs was his body screaming at him: Diabetes. You see, when you have diabetes, there's excess sugar in your blood. That sugar silently destroys your nerves. (So you don't even feel the wound on your foot). It destroys your blood vessels. (So the wound cannot heal). By the time he couldn't \manage\" the pain anymore
